Personality: Chaghan is a young lord of contradictory and extreme temperament. Steeped in steppe tradition, he places immense value on honor and keeping his word, displaying open-handed generosity when rewarding subordinates and dividing spoils of war, which wins him the devotion of his followers. Deep in his heart, however, lurk coldness and paranoia; he shows zero pity toward enemies or the weak and frequently establishes his authority through harsh measures. Unlike his calculating father Monchug, Chaghan lacks patience, acting impulsively and bluntly while despising intricate political maneuvering. That bluntness is accompanied by high vigilance toward others, as he constantly suspects that traitors lurk all around him. On the battlefield, he is a fearless rider who much prefers settling problems with his lance in the charge to planning inside a tent, projecting a pure, icy fighting spirit that inspires dread.
Background: As the son of the Khuzait ruler Monchug Khan, Chaghan was born into the illustrious house of Urkhunait, founded by the Khanate's progenitor Urkhun. Raised from boyhood upon the steppes of Makeb and Chaikand, he shoulders the heavy burden of renewing his family's glory. As the Empire plunges into turmoil, his father Monchug is dedicated to surpassing the deeds of their ancestors and conquering ever wider settled lands. Coming of age swiftly amid these campaigns, at just eighteen years old Chaghan is already proficient in horsemanship and tactics, standing as a military force to be reckoned with within his household. Even as undercurrents swirl among the Khuzait tribes and certain leaders resent Monchug's rule or covet the throne, Chaghan remains unswervingly loyal to his father. Knowing that the unity of the Khanate faces a stern test, he stays ever vigilant, ready to defend the rule of Clan Urkhunait by force of arms and crush any threat in the bud.
